options.plan: Staging; testing only, no account or production entitlement verified
options.region: No environment region selected; storage destinations not verified
options.configuration: Custom SCIM v2.0 inbound to WorkOS; bearer auth; app-owned Events API bridge and state reconciliation; no login

conditions: Staging connections are not billed according to https://workos.com/docs/authkit/environments; production Directory Sync has per-connection charges at https://workos.com/pricing. AuthKit's free user allowance is not free production Directory Sync.

Create an organization-bound Custom SCIM v2.0 directory and configure the upstream provisioner with its WorkOS endpoint and generated bearer token. No account, connector or upstream provider was tested.

WorkOS receives inbound SCIM; the application consumes read-only directory data and implements its own lifecycle, permissions and local-session revocation. This is not a native SCIM endpoint in the SaaS or write-back to the upstream directory: https://workos.com/docs/directory-sync/quick-start.

The app-owned bridge must persist an Events API cursor, handle replay safely and reconcile state; see https://workos.com/docs/events/data-syncing/events-api. No bridge implementation or end-to-end latency was verified.

Inactive users are removed from the WorkOS directory by default, not necessarily deleted from the SaaS. Retaining inactive users requires a separate support-enabled configuration: https://workos.com/docs/directory-sync/handle-inactive-users.

evidence.summary: The custom SCIM guide describes an inbound directory endpoint and selectable request authentication for user/group ingestion. This staging proposal selects bearer authentication and requires application-side integration, not tested deprovisioning.

conditions: Limit this proposal to the same staging Custom SCIM v2.0 directory described at https://workos.com/docs/integrations/scim; it does not establish other connectors, production entitlement or nested-group behavior.

Consume group and membership events through the app-owned bridge. Group deletion does not emit individual dsync.group.user_removed events; remove the deleted group's memberships/access explicitly without assuming every member's account must be deleted.

Reconcile paginated memberships using directory APIs; user updated_at does not change on membership changes. The deprecated Directory User groups field is not a reliable membership inventory: https://workos.com/docs/directory-sync/quick-start.

Map directory and organization identities into application membership and authorization. Group data alone does not enforce roles, remove other memberships or revoke local sessions; no application bridge or lifecycle flow was tested.

evidence.summary: Directory Sync documents group/membership events, group-deletion cleanup and state reconciliation. Configurable group ingestion is distinct from application authorization and does not prove complete or timely access revocation.
